goal: Scaffold monokl's compilable v0.1.0 skeleton for the first time: the workspace root Cargo.toml (Section 28), the monokl crate's own Cargo.toml (Section 1), and lib.rs's module declarations (Section 2), exactly as SPEC-004 locks them.
architecture: Two files are built bottom-up, section by section, each addition verified by an offline text-exactness test (grep/diff against the verbatim source block) rather than a live `cargo build`, because two documented gaps in this spec's own corpus (AC-008B: no `.cargo/config.toml [registries.orin-cargo]` entry anywhere in docs/spec/*.md; and io-errors, the ../io-errors path dependency, not existing anywhere in this workspace) make `cargo metadata`/`build`/`check` against the real crate manifest permanently unable to resolve once AC-008's `registry = "orin-cargo"` line is written -- confirmed empirically: `cargo metadata --no-deps` fails at manifest *parse* time with `registry index was not found in any configuration: \`orin-cargo\`` the instant that key is present, before dependency resolution even begins, regardless of whether io-errors exists on disk. The four behavioral acceptance criteria (AC-001B, AC-003B, AC-008B, AC-025) are instead verified against fully isolated, network-free `/tmp` fixture crates purpose-built to reproduce just the Cargo mechanism in question (required-features gating, publish allow-lists, workspace-inheritance failure, registry resolution) -- every expected error string embedded in this plan's test steps was captured from a real `cargo 1.96.0` run during planning, not guessed. AC-025's positive case (inheritance succeeding) is verified with a self-contained /tmp copy of the finished root Cargo.toml plus a transient probe crate, so the check has no ordering dependency on whether crates/monokl exists yet in the real repo. A final supplementary task (T-023) additionally proves the real assembled manifests parse structurally end-to-end, via a throwaway /tmp copy with only the registry key and io-errors version requirement stripped (both blocked strictly by the two out-of-scope gaps) and a minimal stub io-errors sibling used purely as a path-resolution target. lib.rs's 15 module declarations name 14 pub modules (analysis, budget, cli, dedup, enrich, error, indices, output, pipeline, query, rank, text_search, tokens, types) plus one #[cfg(test)] module (tests_types), none of which exist as files yet -- creating them is explicitly out of this track's scope per SPEC-004's own non_goals ("whose only obligation to this track is to exist as the module lib.rs declares" is a future obligation on those modules' own tracks, not this one), so lib.rs is verified by content-exactness only, never by compiling it.
reasoning: BLOCKING ASSUMPTIONS (stated explicitly per instructions, not deferred): (1) AC-008B documents that no docs/spec/*.md file supplies a `.cargo/config.toml [registries.orin-cargo]` entry -- I independently re-confirmed this is fatal to tooling, not just to `cargo publish`: even `cargo metadata --no-deps` fails at TOML-parse time the moment `registry = "orin-cargo"` appears in any manifest in the workspace, with zero network access attempted. I did NOT fabricate a fake registry config to work around this (that would silently resolve a gap the spec explicitly says is out of corpus and out of this track's scope) -- instead every task touching the real crate/root manifests uses grep/diff text-exactness tests, and every task that needs a live `cargo` process uses an isolated /tmp fixture with no io-errors/registry involvement at all. (2) io-errors itself (the ../io-errors path dependency AC-008 locks) does not exist anywhere in this workspace and creating it is out of scope (non_goals: 'io-errors, or any sibling orin-axi tool' is explicitly excluded) -- so no task in this plan ever runs a real `cargo build`/`check`/`install` against crates/monokl's actual manifest; that only becomes possible once a later, separate track scaffolds crates/io-errors. (3) lib.rs's 14 pub-mod referenced modules (including error/types, whose own tracks SPEC-001/SPEC-003 are already gated) plus the #[cfg(test)] tests_types module do not exist as files; this plan does not create stub files for them since SPEC-004's own non_goals assigns that obligation to each module's own track, not this manifest-locking track -- lib.rs is therefore verified as text only, never compiled, in this plan. VERIFICATION METHODOLOGY: content-locking criteria (AC-001..AC-025 minus the four behavioral/gap ones) are tested via `diff`/`grep -F` against the exact verbatim block quoted in this plan's steps -- offline, deterministic, no cargo invocation, so neither blocking assumption above affects them. The four behavioral criteria (AC-001B, AC-003B, AC-008B, AC-025) and the two cross-file-consistency criteria (AC-015, AC-016) use real `cargo` runs in throwaway /tmp fixtures (AC-001B/003B/008B/025) or grep-based cross-checks between the two real files or the two real docs (AC-015/AC-016) -- every expected error string quoted in those tasks' test steps was reproduced live against cargo 1.96.0 during planning, not invented. Tasks are ordered: workspace root Cargo.toml first (T-001..T-006, since AC-025 proves the crate manifest cannot resolve `.workspace = true` without it), then the crate's own Cargo.toml section-by-section in source order (T-007..T-016), then lib.rs (T-017), then the cross-file consistency checks that need both finished files as reference (T-018 for AC-015, T-019 for AC-016), then the three remaining pure-behavioral criteria in isolated /tmp fixtures (T-020 AC-008B, T-021 AC-001B, T-022 AC-003B) which only need the finished manifest's *content* (already locked by T-001..T-016) as a reference, not the manifest itself, and finally a supplementary structural-parse gate (T-023) that has no covers_criteria of its own since every criterion it touches is already assigned to an earlier task.

' > /tmp/ac003b_fixture2/Cargo.toml && echo 'fn main(){}' > /tmp/ac003b_fixture2/src/main.rs && echo 'pub fn x(){}' > /tmp/ac003b_fixture2/src/lib.rs`. Expected: both fixtures created; no assertions yet.

tasks.title: Structurally validate the assembled real manifests via an offline /tmp copy (supplementary gate)
steps:
Write the failing test. Confirm this task's own verification method (cargo metadata) can actually FAIL on a structurally broken manifest before checking it can succeed on the real one -- a vacuous 'it parses' result wouldn't prove anything, since every prior task (T-001..T-019) verified content only with line-oriented grep/diff windows, which are blind to table structure: a block appended under the wrong preceding header, or a duplicated table header, would satisfy every one of those checks while producing a manifest Cargo itself rejects. (Caveat, scoped precisely: cargo metadata also silently drops a [[bench]] target whose source file does not exist, with no warning -- so this task's parse gate does NOT independently validate [[bench]]'s structural placement; that remains covered only by T-016's line-window diff and this task's own whole-file source diff in the green step below, not by parsing.) Build a deliberately broken copy to prove the gate can fail: `rm -rf /tmp/mk_struct_broken && mkdir -p /tmp/mk_struct_broken/src && printf '[package]
name = "repro"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[package]
name = "repro-dup"
' > /tmp/mk_struct_broken/Cargo.toml && echo 'pub fn x(){}' > /tmp/mk_struct_broken/src/lib.rs`. Assert: `out=$( (cd /tmp/mk_struct_broken && cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1) 2>&1); rc=$?; [ "$rc" != 0 ] && echo BROKEN_REJECTED`. Expected: `BROKEN_REJECTED`.
Confirm red: run the command above now. It prints `BROKEN_REJECTED`, proving the parse gate genuinely discriminates a broken structure from a valid one. Clean up: `rm -rf /tmp/mk_struct_broken`.

Write the minimal implementation. Copy the real files into a throwaway workspace, stripping only the two keys that require environment configuration this track's non_goals excludes (`registry = "orin-cargo"` and the io-errors `version` req, since no real io-errors crate exists to satisfy a version requirement), and add a minimal stub io-errors sibling purely as a path-resolution target (not a specification of io-errors' own content, which is explicitly out of scope): `rm -rf /tmp/mk_struct && mkdir -p /tmp/mk_struct/crates/io-errors/src /tmp/mk_struct/crates/monokl/src && cp /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/Cargo.toml /tmp/mk_struct/Cargo.toml && sed 's#^io-errors = .*#io-errors = { path = "../io-errors", default-features = false }#' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml > /tmp/mk_struct/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml && cp /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/lib.rs /tmp/mk_struct/crates/monokl/src/lib.rs && printf '[package]
name = "io-errors"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
name = "io_errors"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[features]
miette = []
' > /tmp/mk_struct/crates/io-errors/Cargo.toml && echo 'pub fn y(){}' > /tmp/mk_struct/crates/io-errors/src/lib.rs`.

Confirm green. Run: `( (cd /tmp/mk_struct && cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1) > /tmp/mk_meta.json 2>&1 ); echo "exit=$?"` -- expect `exit=0` (the whole assembled manifest -- [package], [lib], [[bin]], [features], [dependencies], [dev-dependencies], [[bench]] as a mechanical table (not independently structure-validated, per the caveat above), [lints], and the root's [workspace.package]/[workspace.lints.*]/[workspace.dependencies] -- parses and resolves offline with no network access). Then assert its content: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/mk_meta.json')); p=[p for p in d['packages'] if p['name']=='monokl'][0]; assert set(p['features'].keys())=={'default','lang-ts','cli','miette'}, p['features'].keys(); assert p['edition']=='2024', p['edition']; assert p['rust_version']=='1.96', p['rust_version']; assert p['license']=='AGPL-3.0-or-later', p['license']; nondev=[d for d in p['dependencies'] if d['kind'] is None]; assert len(nondev)==22, len(nondev); print('OK')"`. Expected: `OK` (22 = 14 always-on core crates + io-errors + 5 optional oxc_* + clap + miette). Also re-confirm whole-file exactness on the real crate manifest against its source document, anchored by pattern rather than a hardcoded line range so the check survives unrelated edits elsewhere in that 3000+ line document, with a length guard so a moved/renamed section fails loudly instead of silently diffing against the wrong content: `block=$(awk '/^# Section 1: Cargo\.toml/{f=1;next} f&&/^```toml$/{c=1;next} c&&/^```$/{exit} c' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md); n=$(echo "$block" | wc -l | tr -d ' '); [ "$n" -eq 86 ] || echo 'SOURCE BLOCK MOVED -- re-derive extraction pattern, got '"$n"' lines, expected 86'; echo "$block" | diff - /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml`. Expected: no SOURCE BLOCK MOVED line, and the diff produces no output, exit 0. Finally, complete AC-023's two-way completeness match on the crate side (T-005 only checked the root side): `grep -cE '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ +=  *\{ workspace = true' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml` expect `27` (26 distinct crates, serde_json counted twice across [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies]), and `diff <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ +=  *\{ workspace = true' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/Cargo.toml | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u) <(sed -n '/^\[workspace.dependencies\]$/,$p' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/Cargo.toml | grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ =' | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u)` expect no output, exit 0 (every crate the crate manifest marks `{ workspace = true }` has a root pin, and vice versa). Clean up: `rm -rf /tmp/mk_struct /tmp/mk_meta.json`.
Commit (no file changes; run `git commit --allow-empty -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` using this task's commit_message, recording the verification as an empty commit).
